meta.titre: Narrative Essay in French: telling an event in three clear paragraphs
meta.sous_theme: Planning from the bullets, passé composé and imparfait, linking words

sections.contenu_markdown: When a thief is caught in a neighbourhood, everyone who was there can tell the story, and each person tells it in an order that the listener can follow: what happened, how people reacted, how it ended. In Paper 2 the examiner asks you to do the same in French, usually about an event in your family, your school or your quarter, and the topic gives you three bullet points to answer. A story that follows the bullets in order, with the right past tenses, can score well even with simple sentences. This course shows how to plan and write it.

items: The passé composé is made of avoir or être in the present plus a past participle (*j'ai mangé*, *elle est partie*).
The imparfait describes a situation or a habit in the past (*il faisait chaud*).
A paragraph groups sentences about one idea and starts on a new line.

sections.titre: Planning and writing a narrative essay in French
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Read the topic

The topic gives a situation and **three bullet points**. They are your plan. Each bullet is one paragraph, answered in the order given. If you forget one, a whole part of the topic is missing.

| Part | Content |
|---|---|
| Short opening | Place, time, who was there (at the start of paragraph 1) |
| Paragraph 1 | First bullet: what happened and where |
| Paragraph 2 | Second bullet: the reactions or the events that follow |
| Paragraph 3 | Third bullet: the ending and, if asked, your feelings or what you learned |

### Tenses of the story

| Use | Tense | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Background, description, feelings | imparfait | Il faisait chaud. J'avais peur. |
| Main action that happens once | passé composé | Soudain, j'ai entendu un cri. |
| Action before the main past action | plus-que-parfait | Il avait plu la veille. |

Past participles: with **être** the participle agrees with the subject (*ma sœur est tombée*, *nous sommes partis*); with **avoir** it agrees with a direct object placed before (*je l'ai emmenée*, if I took my sister).

### Linking words

*D'abord, ensuite, puis, alors, soudain, tout à coup, quelques minutes plus tard, pendant ce temps, enfin, finalement, heureusement, malheureusement.*

### Good habits

- Write short sentences that you control. A correct short sentence earns more than a long wrong one.
- Never translate an English sentence word for word; think in French with the words you know.
- Keep time to read again: verb endings, accents, agreement.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a quoted sentence makes the scene lively
variantes.contenu_markdown: Put the spoken words between guillemets and keep the verb of speech in the passé composé or the imparfait: *« Au secours ! » a crié une dame.* Use a few lines only. The story must stay a story, not a play.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a bullet asks for your reaction or what you learned
variantes.contenu_markdown: Describe the feeling with the imparfait (*j'étais inquiet, j'avais peur*) and give its cause with *parce que* or *car*. Close with a lesson in the present: *Cette journée m'a appris que la solidarité est précieuse.*

sections.enonce_markdown:
(a) You witnessed a fire in your quarter.

- Say how the fire started and what you did.
- Say how the neighbours reacted.
- Say how the situation ended.

etapes.justification: The topic is a story of the past in the first person, and it has three bullets. Three paragraphs are needed, in that order.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Narrative in the past, first person, 3 paragraphs.

etapes.justification: A plan keeps the order and gives the same weight to each bullet.
etapes.resultat_markdown: P1 start of the fire and my action. P2 neighbours' reactions. P3 firemen, ending, lesson.

etapes.action: Write paragraph 1: set the scene with the imparfait, then the main actions with the passé composé.
etapes.justification: Imparfait for the background, passé composé for the events that make the story move.
etapes.resultat_markdown: *C'était un samedi après-midi et il faisait très chaud dans notre quartier à Bafoussam. Ma mère préparait le repas quand j'ai senti une odeur de fumée. Je suis sorti et j'ai vu de grandes flammes dans la maison d'un voisin. J'ai crié de toutes mes forces : « Au feu ! Au feu ! »*

etapes.justification: A linking word shows the order of events; the reactions are described with the imparfait when they last.
etapes.resultat_markdown: *Aussitôt, les voisins sont arrivés en courant avec des seaux d'eau. Certains avaient peur et reculaient, d'autres essayaient d'éteindre le feu. Une dame pleurait parce qu'elle ne retrouvait pas son petit garçon. Heureusement, un jeune homme l'a retrouvé derrière la maison.*

etapes.action: Write paragraph 3 and check the participles.
etapes.justification: The ending answers the third bullet and the plus-que-parfait shows what had happened before the arrival.
etapes.resultat_markdown: *Quand les pompiers sont arrivés, le feu avait déjà détruit une partie du toit. Ils ont vite maîtrisé l'incendie et personne n'a été blessé. Le soir, tout le quartier s'est réuni pour aider la famille. Cette journée m'a appris que la solidarité est très précieuse.*

sections.conclusion_markdown: The three paragraphs above, put one after the other, form the model essay. Each bullet is answered in order; the background uses the imparfait (*il faisait, préparait, avaient peur*), the events use the passé composé (*j'ai senti, sont arrivés*), the earlier fact uses the plus-que-parfait (*avait détruit*), and linking words (*aussitôt, heureusement, quand*) guide the reader.

items.erreur_markdown: *Hier, je vais au marché et je rencontre un ami.* (FALSE: tenses mixed)
items.pourquoi_faux: The adverb *hier* shows a past event, but the verbs are in the present. A narrative must use past tenses throughout.
items.correction_markdown: *Hier, je suis allé au marché et j'ai rencontré un ami.*

items.pourquoi_faux: *Tomber* is conjugated with être in the passé composé, and the participle agrees with the subject.

items.erreur_markdown: *Soudain, la porte s'ouvrait et un homme entrait.* (FALSE use of tenses)
items.pourquoi_faux: *Soudain* introduces a sudden action that happens once, which needs the passé composé, not the imparfait.
items.correction_markdown: *Soudain, la porte s'est ouverte et un homme est entré.*

items.erreur_markdown: *J'ai pris ma sœur à l'hôpital.* (FALSE French)
items.pourquoi_faux: This is an English calque ("I took my sister"). *Prendre* does not mean to take a person somewhere.

items.erreur_markdown: A candidate describes the illness in detail but never says where the child was taken or how it ended.
items.pourquoi_faux: The bullets are part of the topic. Leaving out a bullet means a part of the topic is not answered, and the content is incomplete.
items.correction_markdown: Answer every bullet, one paragraph each and in the order given.

items.enonce_markdown:
Put the verb in brackets in the correct tense (passé composé or imparfait).

(a) Hier, ma sœur (aller) au marché.
(b) Hier soir, j'(manger) du riz.
(c) Il (pleuvoir) quand je suis sorti.
(d) Tout à coup, un chien (traverser) la route.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **est allée.** Aller takes être, and the participle agrees with the feminine subject.

(b) **ai mangé.** A single finished action: passé composé with avoir.

(c) **pleuvait.** The rain is the background situation, so the imparfait.

(d) **a traversé.** *Tout à coup* introduces a sudden action: passé composé.

items.enonce_markdown:
Rewrite the following text in the past, with the imparfait and the passé composé:

*Je marche vers l'école. Il fait chaud. Soudain, j'entends un cri. Je cours vers la rue et je vois un enfant qui pleure.*
items.solution_markdown:
**Je marchais vers l'école. Il faisait chaud. Soudain, j'ai entendu un cri. J'ai couru vers la rue et j'ai vu un enfant qui pleurait.**

Award a mark for each correct verb: *marchais* and *faisait* (background, imparfait); *ai entendu*, *ai couru* and *ai vu* (events, passé composé); *pleurait* (a situation in progress).

items.enonce_markdown:
Topic: (a) A classmate was hurt during a football match at school.

- Describe the circumstances of the accident.
- Say how classmates and teachers reacted.
- Say how the matter ended.

Write a plan in three lines, then the first paragraph (four or five sentences).
items.solution_markdown:
Plan: **P1** the match and the accident; **P2** reactions of classmates and teachers; **P3** hospital or first aid, ending and lesson.

Model first paragraph:

*C'était un mercredi après-midi et notre classe jouait un match de football contre une autre classe. Il avait plu pendant la nuit et l'herbe était encore mouillée. Vers la fin du match, Tabi a couru derrière le ballon, mais il a glissé et il est tombé lourdement. Il a poussé un cri de douleur et il n'a plus pu se relever.*

Award a mark for each of these: the plan follows the three bullets; the scene uses the imparfait (*jouait, était*); the events use the passé composé (*a couru, a glissé, est tombé*); the plus-que-parfait is correct (*avait plu*); spelling, accents and agreement are correct.

items_markdown: Each bullet of the topic is one paragraph, in the order given. Never leave a bullet unanswered.
Imparfait for background and feelings, passé composé for the events that move the story, plus-que-parfait for what happened before.
With être the past participle agrees with the subject (elle est tombée); with avoir it agrees with a direct object placed before the verb.
Use linking words (d'abord, soudain, heureusement, enfin) and short sentences that you can write correctly.
Do not translate from English word for word, and keep time to read again for verb endings, accents and agreement.
